extracted.intended_audience: pilots, air carriers, flight procedure designers, airspace/charting stakeholders, and FAA/regulatory staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule amendments to 14 CFR part 95 specifying required IFR (instrument flight rules) minimum/maximum en route altitudes, changeover points, and related navigation/equipment designators for Federal airways, RNAV routes, jet routes, and direct routes; includes legal/administrative findings supporting immediate effectiveness and incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material Incorporated by Reference (IBR) approval and mandatory use
rubrics_metrics.description: (k)(1) The Director of the Federal Register approved the incorporation by reference (IBR) of the material listed in this paragraph under 5 U.S.C. 552(a) and 1 CFR part 51. (k)(2) You must use this material as applicable to do the actions required by this AD, unless the AD specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific IBR item(s) (example: GE CF34—10E Service Bulletin 72-0351 R01, dated July 17, 2019). Provides contact information for the material holder (GE) and instructions on where to view the material (FAA Airworthiness Products Section, Operational Safety Branch; National Archives and Records Administration with URL and email). The incorporated material, once approved, is mandatory for compliance unless the AD explicitly says otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and availability of IBR materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For GE material identified in this AD, contact GE at provided address/phone/email/website; view the material at the FAA Airworthiness Products Section (phone provided) or at NARA (visit provided URL or email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact contact points: GE, 1 Neumann Way, Cincinnati, OH 45215; phone: (513) 552-3272; email: aviation.fleetsupport@ge.com; website: ge.com. FAA viewing: Airworthiness Products Section, Operational Safety Branch, 1200 District Avenue, Burlington, MA 01803 (call (817) 222-5110 for availability). NARA viewing info: www.archives.gov/federal-register/cfr/ibr-locations or fr.inspection@nara.gov. Use these channels to obtain materials mandatory under the IBR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective-date timing and need for expedited effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: This amendment is made effective at 0901 UTC on a specified date (example: June 12, 2025) because changes must be available to users before the next scheduled charting and publication date to assure timely availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains that the effective date is chosen to ensure the amendments are available to users in time for charting/publication; the close and immediate relationship between these regulatory changes and safety in air commerce justifies making the amendment effective in less than 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause finding for bypassing prior notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA finds that notice and public procedure before adopting this amendment are impracticable and contrary to the public interest and that good cause exists for making the amendment effective in less than 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the amendments address matters of flight safety and operational efficiency in the National Airspace System and are closely and immediately related to safety in air commerce. Where timing is critical to ensure safe/efficient navigation and chart availability, the agency may invoke the good-cause exception to standard notice-and-comment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory significance and economic-impact determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA determined the regulation involves an established body of technical regulations for which frequent and routine amendments are necessary to keep them operationally current; therefore the amendment is (1) not a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866; (2) not a 'significant rule' under DOT policies; and (3) does not warrant preparation of a regulatory evaluation and will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations are used to justify reduced analytic/economic paperwork and certification; they reflect the agency's assessment that operational technical amendments carry minimal broader economic impact and are routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and safety/efficiency standard for IFR altitudes and changeover points
rubrics_metrics.description: The specified IFR altitudes, when used in conjunction with the prescribed changeover points for those routes, ensure navigation aid coverage that is adequate for safe flight operations and free of frequency interference; they provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must address navigation coverage adequacy and avoidance of frequency interference; they should be related to published aeronautical charts essential to users. Changes are driven by reasons/circumstances tied to flight safety and operational efficiency and must be reflected in charting/publication promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation requirement for amending part 95
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to 14 CFR part 95 must be made pursuant to the cited statutory/regulatory authority: 49 U.S.C. 106(g), 40103, 40113 and 14 CFR 11.49(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every amendment includes an authority citation that establishes the FAA's legal basis for the regulatory changes; this citation must be included in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and labeling of altitudes, equipment-dependent MEAs, and route constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Route amendments specify From/To fixes and list MEA (minimum en route altitude) and MAA (maximum authorized altitude) values and may annotate altitudes with equipment or navigation-source designators such as '*18000—GNSS MEA', '*DME/DME/IRU MEA', '*2500—MOCA', '*9300—MCA', '*5000—MRA', or mark fixes/routes as 'UNUSABLE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables/route entries must clearly indicate the applicable altitude value and, where required, the navigation/equipment method that establishes the MEA (e.g., GNSS MEA vs. DME/DME/IRU MEA). Entries may also show special notes (e.g., 'UNUSABLE', 'UNUSABLE BELOW X') and boundary-specific annotations (E/W/NW/SE BND). These designators inform pilots/operators which navigation equipment or signal coverage is required to meet the altitude and routing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to keep technical airspace regulations operationally current
rubrics_metrics.description: This regulation is part of an established body of technical regulations that require frequent and routine amendments to remain operationally current for safe and efficient use of the National Airspace System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of operational needs and charting cycles, the FAA regularly updates routing and altitude tables; such updates must be coordinated with publication/charting schedules and implemented promptly to ensure users have current information.
